notes: Per-page performance budgets for the dashboard. Two independent rules judge every metric: an absolute ceiling (what acceptable means) and a band around the route's own baseline (what got worse). Only page_bytes is baselined, and it is near-deterministic rather than exact: the navigation response carries a fresh CSP nonce per request, so an encoded page moves by a few bytes between requests -- five bytes across fifteen requests to /, against a 10 percent band. Every subresource is byte-identical every time. page_bytes is otherwise a property of the build rather than of the data: the dashboard is a static export, so a navigation returns a prebuilt page from the binary and every subresource is a content-hashed file beside it, while run data arrives over the API after load. Two pages carry the recharts chunks and are heavy for that reason; the rest differ by a few kilobytes of route code. /runs sits at 90 percent of the ceiling with recharts already route-split, so the next page that draws a chart ships over the ceiling and needs a smaller charting dependency rather than another split. Every number was measured over the wire against a served listener with the encoding the server offers a browser, which is what a page-weight budget means; the same pages unencoded measure 732,498 to 1,475,205 bytes and every one of them breaches the ceiling. /docs is the one baselined page served unencoded. internal/web imports internal/docsweb, so sharing the encoder means moving it to a third package, and at 7 percent of the ceiling that buys nothing. The timings are unmeasured: this repository has no browser sweep of its own, and numbers taken on a machine running parallel gates would bake that in. No check in this repository reads this file. It is written for a scheduled browser sweep that lives elsewhere, in the shape overwing and bitwing use, so a reader can tell an unenforced manifest from a stale one. Any tool reading this file must check version and refuse one it does not implement: unknown keys decode to zero, so a reader meeting a newer schema sees routes with no baselines, which is indistinguishable from routes nobody has baselined.

corpora.local: The dashboard as `sparkwing serve` serves it from a freshly created SPARKWING_HOME, measured with `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br`. page_bytes is the navigation response plus every subresource the page references, so it does not move with the runs in the store; it moves with the bundle `bin/build-web.sh` produces. It is the only corpus sparkwing has for this metric.
